12.t: Working with data: sorting a class
q: How many pencil cases had a zip?
How many pencil cases had a zip AND were made of fabric?
Explain why "nice colour" would be a poor feature to sort by.
It is an opinion: different people would sort the same pencil case differently, so the groups would not be the same each time.
After split 3 there are four groups. Explain why the pencil cases in each group are more alike than at the start, and suggest how many more splits are needed so every case is alone.

Each split adds one more shared feature, so members of a group share more features (e.g. zip + fabric). With 24 cases, each split can at best halve a group: 24, 12, 6, 3, 2, 1, so about 5 splits in total at least (more if groups are uneven).
